# A session's messages are stored whole, and threads group them

Every line a harness writes for a session is stored as a **message**, whole and untouched, the way the Claude Agent SDK's `SessionStore` mirrors a transcript ("persist them in order and return them from `load` in the same order", [Claude Agent SDK](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/session-storage#write-your-own-adapter)), so a session resumes from the factory's database rather than from the harness's own file, which the harness deletes on its own ("The sweep deletes transcripts without showing a message", [Claude Code](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/settings-reference#cleanupperioddays)). A message keeps its `sessionId`, its place in its file of that session (`sessionSeq`, with `subpath` naming the file of a subagent the harness started itself) and its `type`. A **thread** groups the messages about one thing the human asked, across sessions, through `threadId` and `threadSeq`, and holds only what changes about it: its `title`, and the human's `lastReadAt`, `pinnedAt` and `archivedAt`, from which the **Inbox** counts unread messages. A thread keeps no `sessionId`: its messages can come from several sessions, so it belongs to no single session, as [ADR 0004](0004-threads-not-sessions.md) has it. Each new message is routed to the thread it follows up, or starts a new one. A session also keeps `harnessSessionId`, the session id the harness gives it, which the harness takes back to resume it. The names follow the consensus in the [research](../research/0004-threads-messages-and-inbox.md): thread for a conversation kept apart inside a session, message for the record, `seq` for its order, route for sending a message to its thread, and Inbox and unread for the view. Compaction is the harness's own for now, and its lines are messages like any other; a successor that takes over before the context fills, compactions compared across compactors, and the run record they need are left for later. A thread's status waits for the harness, read state kept per person waits for a second human (until then `lastReadAt` is the one human's), and whether a message one agent sends another is tagged with its thread on both sides waits for how agents message each other.

## Considered Options

- **One table for lines and threads alike:** a thread's title and read state change every time the human opens it, while a message is never changed once written, so the two stay apart, as Mastra, Codex, the OpenAI Conversations API and Cloudflare keep a conversation apart from its messages.
- **The harness's own names (`TranscriptEntry`, `entry`, `runId`):** the record has to fit every harness, so it takes the consensus names; only `subpath`, which no other source has, keeps the Claude Agent SDK's word.
- **Role, time and parent as columns:** they are inside `content` already, and the UUID version 7 `id` holds the time, so only `type`, which every view filters on, is a column.
- **A run record now:** it only matters while two starts of one session overlap, which happens only in a handover.
